current_bottleneck: 287c validated that splitting the retrieval key into fast and slow channels restores the missing slow structure. The remaining miss is now narrower: the replay support and future key live in a local-history z-coordinate, but the query/history key is still built from globally normalized levels. That query/support coordinate mismatch appears to be what still degrades active-cell mean reversion and local structural robustness.
last_result_summary: Iteration 113 ran 287c-v0 and got 4/11. It improved 287b materially on cointegration, aggregate mean reversion, rank structure, and level KS while preserving strong change KS, but it still failed active-cell mean-reversion support, time-series skew/tail details, and pathwise jump realism. This makes 287c the cleanest result so far in the 287 family, but 277d remains the stronger deterministic Stage A frontier at 5/11.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 287d-v0 as the smallest query-coordinate fix: keep the 287c fast/slow split and normalized-change replay support fixed, but build the history/query channels in the same local-history z-coordinate used by the replay support.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
